title: Supply Chain Management
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Una idea brillante no sirve de nada si no puedes fabricarla y entregarla. Entender la Cadena de Suministro te permite hablar sobre cómo los productos globales llegan desde la fábrica hasta las manos del cliente.

stages.title: Gestión de la Cadena de Suministro (C2)

parts.visual:
En negocios internacionales, la logística lo es todo. Conoce estos términos: 

1. Supply Chain (Cadena de suministro): 
- Toda la red de personas y empresas involucradas en crear y vender un producto. 
Ej: The global pandemic caused massive disruptions in the SUPPLY CHAIN. 

2. Just-in-Time / JIT (Justo a tiempo): 
- Un sistema donde los materiales llegan exactamente cuando se necesitan para la producción, ahorrando costos de almacén. 
Ej: Toyota pioneered the JUST-IN-TIME manufacturing system. 

3. Backlog (Trabajo acumulado / Pedidos pendientes): 
- Una acumulación de trabajo o pedidos que aún no se han procesado. 
Ej: We have a huge BACKLOG of orders due to the factory strike.
parts.audio: Welcome to Supply Chain Management. In international business, logistics is everything. Number 1: Supply Chain. The entire network of entities, people, and resources involved in creating and selling a product. For example: The global pandemic caused massive disruptions in the SUPPLY CHAIN. Number 2: Just-in-Time, or JIT. An inventory system where materials arrive exactly when they are needed in the production process, reducing storage costs. For example: Toyota pioneered the JUST-IN-TIME manufacturing system. Number 3: Backlog. An accumulation of uncompleted work or customer orders waiting to be processed. For example: We have a huge BACKLOG of orders due to the factory strike.

parts.visual:
4. Bottleneck (Cuello de botella): 
- Un punto de congestión en un sistema que frena todo el proceso. 
Ej: The quality control department has become a massive BOTTLENECK. 

5. Procurement (Adquisiciones / Compras): 
- El proceso corporativo de encontrar y comprar bienes y servicios de proveedores. 
Ej: Our PROCUREMENT team is negotiating a new contract for steel. 

6. Lead time (Tiempo de entrega / Tiempo de ciclo): 
- El tiempo que transcurre entre hacer un pedido y recibirlo. 
Ej: If we order from China, the LEAD TIME is six weeks. 

7. Outsourcing (Subcontratación / Externalización): 
- Contratar a terceros (a menudo en otro país) para hacer un trabajo. 
Ej: We are OUTSOURCING our customer service to India.
parts.audio: Number 4: Bottleneck. A point of congestion in a system that slows down the overall process. Like the neck of a bottle. For example: The quality control department has become a massive BOTTLENECK. Number 5: Procurement. The formal corporate process of finding, agreeing terms, and buying goods or services from external sources. For example: Our PROCUREMENT team is negotiating a new contract for steel. Number 6: Lead time. The amount of time that passes from the start of a process, like placing an order, until its conclusion. For example: If we order from China, the LEAD TIME is six weeks. Number 7: Outsourcing. Obtaining goods or services from an outside or foreign supplier. For example: We are OUTSOURCING our customer service to India.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de logística correcto.

questions.question: The earthquake in Taiwan destroyed microchip factories, causing a global ____ chain crisis. (Cadena de suministro).
To save money on warehouses, we use ____-in-time manufacturing, where parts arrive the exact day we build the car.
Because the website crashed for three days, we now have a massive ____ of unprocessed orders. (Acumulación/Pedidos pendientes).
questions.explanation: Backlog = pedidos pendientes o trabajo acumulado.

questions.question: The factory can produce 1000 phones a day, but the packaging team can only box 500. Packaging is a ____. (Cuello de botella).
questions.explanation: Bottleneck = cuello de botella (el punto que frena todo).

questions.question: The ____ department is responsible for finding suppliers and negotiating prices for raw materials. (Compras / Adquisiciones).
questions.explanation: Procurement = el departamento de adquisiciones corporativas.

questions.question: If you order the standard parts, they arrive tomorrow. For custom parts, the ____ time is 3 months. (Tiempo de entrega).
questions.explanation: Lead time = tiempo de entrega (desde el pedido hasta la recepción).

questions.question: Instead of hiring an internal accounting team, they decided on ____ the work to a firm in the Philippines. (Subcontratar).
Relocating business processes to another country, often to lower costs, is specifically called ____. (Deslocalización).
questions.explanation: Offshoring = mover operaciones a otro país (puede ser tu propia empresa, no siempre subcontratado).

questions.question: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold, such as copper or coffee, is a ____. (Materia prima/Producto básico).
questions.explanation: Commodity = producto básico (petróleo, trigo, cobre, etc.).

questions.question: All the goods and materials that a business holds for the ultimate goal of resale or production is its ____. (Inventario).
The physical building where goods are stored before distribution is a ____. (Almacén).
Moving goods from the manufacturer directly to the customer, bypassing the retailer, is called 'Direct to ____' (D2C).
The very final step of the delivery process, from a distribution center to the customer's front door, is called the 'last ____'. (Última milla).
questions.explanation: Last-mile delivery = la entrega de última milla (la parte más cara de la logística).

questions.question: The people or companies that supply raw materials to your company are your ____. (Proveedores).
The management of the flow of things between the point of origin and the point of consumption is called ____. (Logística).
A situation where a company runs completely out of a specific product and cannot fulfill orders is a ____-out. (Desabastecimiento).
questions.explanation: Stock-out = falta de existencias (quedarse sin stock).

questions.question: A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports is a ____. (Arancel).
Bringing manufacturing jobs back to your own country from overseas is called ____. (Relocalización).
questions.explanation: Reshoring (u onshoring) = volver a traer las fábricas al país de origen.

questions.question: The cost associated with storing unsold inventory in a warehouse is called the 'carrying ____'. (Costo de mantenimiento).
questions.explanation: Carrying cost = el costo de almacenar inventario no vendido.

questions.question: A company that provides logistics services (transportation, warehousing) to another company is a 'Third-Party Logistics' provider, or ____.
____ chain. (Cadena de suministro con S)
____-in-time. (Justo a tiempo con J)
A massive ____. (Acumulación de pedidos con B)
A production ____. (Cuello de botella con B)
The ____ team. (Departamento de adquisiciones/compras con P)
A long ____ time. (Tiempo de entrega con L)
____ services. (Subcontratar con O)
A raw ____. (Producto básico/materia prima con C)
The last ____. (Entrega final con M)
Our ____ in China. (Proveedores con S)

pairs.target: Cuello de botella en el proceso
Tiempo desde el pedido hasta la entrega
El paso final para llegar a la casa del cliente
